frontMatter.introduction:
Alchem International Private Limited is a leading manufacturer in the pharmaceutical, phytochemical, botanical extraction, nutraceutical, and cosmeceutical ingredient industry, specializing in high-quality plant-derived active ingredients and APIs for global pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and nutraceutical brands. With extensive experience in botanical extraction, isolation, purification, synthesis, and finishing, Alchem International is committed to product quality, responsible production, worker welfare, and environmentally conscious operations across its manufacturing facilities.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual has been developed to ensure that all operational activities across the organization are carried out in a consistent, safe, and efficient manner, while meeting applicable legal, customer, and regulatory requirements. The manual establishes a unified operational framework that supports Alchem International's manufacturing processes—from botanical raw material sourcing and production planning to extraction, isolation, purification, quality control, packing, and dispatch—while reinforcing compliance with occupational health and safety, environmental management, and social responsibility standards relevant to the pharmaceutical and phytochemical sector.

The SOP Manual serves as a comprehensive reference for employees, supervisors, managers, and technical personnel by clearly defining roles, responsibilities, and standardized work practices. It promotes operational discipline, ethical conduct, product consistency, and continuous improvement, thereby strengthening Alchem International's commitment to responsible manufacturing, workplace safety, and long-term sustainability across all its operations.

frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
SOP MANUAL REVIEW MECHANISM

The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual at Alchem International Private Limited is a living document. It must evolve with changes in regulations, technology, customer expectations, operational processes, and organizational structure. An outdated SOP is not merely ineffective—it can create compliance risks, safety hazards, and operational inefficiencies.

This SOP Manual Review Mechanism establishes a structured, periodic, and trigger-based review process to ensure that all SOPs remain current, relevant, effective, and compliant with applicable Bangladesh labour laws, corporate regulations, and industry best practices.

This mechanism supports operational consistency, risk management, and continuous improvement across all functions at Alchem International.

Purpose and Objectives
The purpose of this procedure is to:

Ensure the SOP Manual remains current, relevant, and effective.
Comply with applicable Indian labour laws, corporate regulations, and industry best practices.
Identify and remove outdated or redundant procedures.
Integrate employee feedback and operational insights.
Strengthen governance, risk control, and operational alignment.
Support audit readiness and customer compliance.
Drive continuous improvement across all functions.

Scope and Applicability
This SOP applies to all SOPs contained within the Alchem International SOP Manual, covering:

Manufacturing operations
Quality control and quality assurance
Environmental, health, and safety (EHS)
Human resources and administration
Procurement and supply chain
Information technology and data management
Finance and compliance
Sustainability and ESG
Any other documented procedure

It applies to all departments, functions, and personnel involved in developing, reviewing, approving, or implementing SOPs.

Organizational Responsibilities
Managing Director / Senior Management: Approves major policy or framework updates. Provides strategic direction for SOP review.
HR Manager: Leads the annual SOP review process. Issues review notifications. Maintains version control. Coordinates with stakeholders.
IT / Systems Manager: Reviews IT operations, data security, and cybersecurity-related SOPs.
Operations Manager: Reviews production processes, operational controls, and efficiency-related SOPs.
EHS Head: Reviews environmental, health, and safety SOPs.
Compliance Head: Reviews regulatory and customer compliance SOPs.
Department Heads: Review departmental SOPs. Provide input on operational changes.
All Employees: Provide feedback on SOP effectiveness and usability.

Review Frequency
1. Annual Comprehensive Review

An annual comprehensive review of the SOP Manual is conducted. All SOPs are reviewed at least once every year to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness.

2. Trigger-Based Reviews

Additional reviews are initiated following significant organizational, regulatory, technological, or operational changes.

Review triggers include
Amendments to Indian labour, environmental, or corporate laws
Changes in regulatory expectations or compliance frameworks
Cybersecurity or data protection risks
Organizational restructuring or process changes
Updates to ISO certifications or management systems
Customer requirement changes
Major audit findings
Significant incidents or accidents
Introduction of new products, processes, or equipment
Technology upgrades
Feedback from employees, customers, or auditors

Review Process
Step 1: Review Notification

The HR Department issues a formal review notification to relevant stakeholders at least one month in advance. The notification includes:

Scope of review
Timeline
Responsibilities
Required inputs

Step 2: Review Meetings

Designated stakeholders review existing SOPs, assess gaps, and propose updates or improvements. Review meetings may be conducted:

Department-wise
Function-wise
Cross-functional (for SOPs affecting multiple departments)

Step 3: Feedback Integration

Employee and departmental feedback is documented, evaluated, and incorporated where relevant. Feedback may be collected through:

Written submissions
Meetings
Surveys
Suggestion boxes
Audit findings

Step 4: SOP Updates

Approved revisions are formally documented and integrated into the SOP Manual with version control. Updates may include:

Minor revisions (typographical, formatting, minor procedural changes)
Major revisions (process changes, regulatory updates, structural changes)
New SOPs
Withdrawal of obsolete SOPs

Step 5: Communication and Training

Updated SOPs are communicated through internal channels, including email and intranet, and training is conducted where required.

Communication includes:

Summary of changes
Rationale for changes
Effective date
Training requirements
Access to updated documents

Documentation and Approval
1. Version Control

All SOP changes are recorded with:

Revision number
Date of revision
Summary of changes
Justification notes
Approving authority

2. Approval Authority

Minor Revisions: Department Head + HR
Major Revisions: Department Head + HR + Managing Director
New SOPs: Department Head + HR + Managing Director
Withdrawal of SOPs: HR + Managing Director

3. Final Approval

The updated SOP Manual receives final approval from the Head of HR before release.

4. Document Control

Master copy maintained by HR
Controlled copies distributed to departments
Obsolete copies withdrawn and destroyed
Digital copies on intranet with version control

Accessibility
The latest approved SOP Manual is:

Available digitally on the company intranet or shared drive
Maintained in physical copies at relevant departmental offices for reference
Accessible to all employees as required for their roles

Training and Awareness
All employees are informed of SOP updates relevant to their roles.
Training is conducted for major revisions.
Training records are maintained by HR.
Awareness sessions are conducted for new SOPs.

Continuous Improvement
Alchem International strengthens its SOP review mechanism through:

Annual review of the review process itself
Integration of feedback from employees, auditors, and customers
Benchmarking against industry best practices
Progressive adoption of digital document management systems
Regular training of SOP owners and reviewers

Compliance
This SOP Manual Review Mechanism aligns with:

Applicable Indian labour and corporate laws
ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 27001
Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
Customer Codes of Conduct
Industry best practices

Documentation and Records
Annual Review Plan: HR, 5 years
Review Meeting Minutes: HR, 5 years
Feedback Records: HR, 5 years
Revision Summaries: HR, 5 years
Approval Records: HR, 5 years
Training Records: HR, 3 years

Master SOP Manual: HR, Current version + 5 years

blocks.text: Alchem International actively integrates circular economy principles and safer chemical management practices into its hazardous waste management framework. The focus is on reducing hazardous waste at source, improving material efficiency, recovering usable inputs, and transitioning to less hazardous and more sustainable alternatives wherever technically and commercially feasible within the pharmaceutical and phytochemical industry.

body.text:
Solvent Recovery & Reuse in Extraction and Purification Operations: Residual solvents from extraction, purification, and synthesis processes are recovered through distillation and purification for reuse where feasible. Controlled reuse of low-risk solvents is carried out after internal verification to reduce fresh solvent consumption and waste generation.
Reuse of Cleaning Solutions: Cleaning solutions used for equipment, reactors, and tools are segregated by type and contamination level. Where quality and safety parameters allow, these solutions are reused for non-critical cleaning or pre-cleaning activities.
Recovery of Packaging Inputs: Chemical drums, containers, and IBCs are cleaned and reused internally where permitted or returned to suppliers under take-back arrangements, reducing hazardous container waste.
ETP By-product Management: Sludge and residues generated from effluent treatment are monitored for calorific value and disposal suitability. Where permitted, co-processing or authorized treatment routes are explored to minimize landfill disposal.
Side Stream Utilization: Wash water or rinse streams with acceptable quality parameters are reused for secondary washing, floor cleaning, or utility purposes, subject to internal controls and regulatory allowances.

Safer Chemical Audits: Periodic reviews are conducted to identify opportunities to replace hazardous chemicals used in extraction, purification, and synthesis with lower-toxicity or environmentally preferable alternatives.
Low-VOC and Water-Based Chemicals: Preference is given to water-based solvents, reagents, and auxiliaries, as well as low volatile organic compound (VOC) formulations, to reduce air emissions and health risks.
Bio-Based and Enzyme-Based Products: Where feasible, bio-based catalysts, enzyme-based reagents, and biodegradable auxiliaries are adopted to reduce chemical load in effluents and hazardous waste streams.
Phosphate-Free and Eco-Labelled Detergents: Phosphate-free detergents and eco-labelled cleaning agents are used in cleaning and equipment maintenance to minimize aquatic toxicity.
Water-Based Degreasers: Maintenance workshops use water-based degreasers for machinery and component cleaning, reducing reliance on petroleum-based solvents.
Sustainable Packaging for Chemicals: Preference is given to suppliers providing chemicals in recyclable, reusable, or returnable packaging such as reusable drums and IBCs, with minimal secondary packaging.

steps.heading: Use of Alternative and Less Hazardous Substances

body.text:
Chemical Substitution: High-hazard chemicals used in extraction, purification, and synthesis are systematically reviewed and replaced with safer alternatives where process performance and product quality are not compromised.
Reduction of Hazardous Additives: Chemicals classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic, reprotoxic, or highly sensitizing are avoided wherever possible, and use is restricted only to essential applications with strict controls.
Elimination of Restricted Substances: Substances restricted under international pharmaceutical standards and customer RSL/MRSL requirements are phased out, with strong monitoring of incoming chemicals.
Reduced Corrosive Chemical Usage: Strong acids and alkalis are replaced with milder formulations in cleaning and finishing processes where feasible, reducing corrosion risks and hazardous effluent loads.

Substitution-First Procurement Policy: The Procurement team follows a substitution-first approach, prioritising suppliers offering safer, environmentally responsible chemical alternatives that meet performance and compliance requirements.
Hazard and Lifecycle Assessment: Chemical sourcing decisions consider hazard classification, environmental fate, and lifecycle impacts, particularly for high-volume extraction and purification chemicals.
Supplier Sustainability Performance: Supplier evaluations include environmental and safety criteria such as reduction of hazardous content, waste minimization initiatives, packaging take-back programs, and regulatory compliance.
Long-Term Responsible Partnerships: Alchem International builds long-term partnerships with suppliers demonstrating strong sustainability credentials, transparent chemical disclosure, and alignment with responsible manufacturing practices.

blocks.text: Proper identification, secure containment, and compliant movement of hazardous waste are critical to minimising risks related to chemical exposure, spills, fire hazards, environmental damage, and regulatory non-compliance. Alchem International has established detailed and rigorous protocols for hazardous waste labelling, storage, handling, and transportation, aligned with applicable Indian environmental regulations (Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016), recognised international chemical safety practices, and customer environmental compliance expectations. These protocols ensure full operational control, traceability, and accountability throughout the hazardous waste lifecycle.

body.text: Each hazardous waste container—whether drum, barrel, carboy, IBC, or bag—is labelled immediately at the point of generation and remains fully traceable until final treatment or disposal.
Labelling Standards
All hazardous waste containers must be labelled in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) and applicable national standards. Labels must be:

Clearly printed, laminated, and weather-resistant
Firmly affixed to the container
Easily visible from all accessible sides
Label Requirements
Each label must include the following information:

Material / Waste Stream Name (e.g., Extraction Residue, Spent Solvent, Used Oil, ETP Sludge)
Chemical Composition / Primary Hazardous Constituents (where applicable)
Physical State (solid / liquid / sludge)
GHS Hazard Class Symbols (flammable, corrosive, toxic, reactive, etc.)
Generating Department & Responsible Contact Person
Accumulation Start Date & Maximum Storage Duration (as per regulatory limits)
Waste Quantity (gross, net, and container weight where applicable)
Proposed Disposal Method (authorised recycler, incineration, secure landfill, co-processing)
Container Identification Number / Barcode
Label Implementation Notes

All labels are bilingual (English and Hindi) to ensure universal understanding.
Barcodes or unique container numbers are logged into the Hazardous Waste Tracking Register or equivalent system maintained by the EHS team.
Internal colour-coded label borders are used as visual identification aids:
Red Border - Toxic or highly hazardous waste
Orange Border - Flammable waste
Yellow Border - Reactive or unstable waste
Black Border - Corrosive waste

In cases where containers are reused (e.g., cleaned chemical drums), all previous labels must be completely removed and destroyed before new labels are applied to prevent misidentification and accidental misuse.
Hazardous waste is stored only in designated, secured, and engineered storage areas designed to prevent leakage, incompatible mixing, fire risk, unauthorised access, and environmental exposure.
Physical Infrastructure Requirements

Chemical-resistant, epoxy-coated flooring to prevent seepage and allow easy cleaning.
Secondary containment systems, bund walls, or spill pallets with a minimum capacity of 110% of the largest container stored.
Fire detection systems, including smoke detectors and heat sensors, connected to the central fire alarm system.
Restricted access controls, allowing entry only to trained and authorised personnel.
Adequate ventilation to prevent accumulation of hazardous vapours.
Intrinsically safe, spark-proof lighting and electrical fittings in areas storing flammable waste.
Storage Management Controls

Hazardous wastes are segregated based on compatibility (e.g., acids separated from alkalis; flammables isolated from oxidisers).
Containers are kept sealed at all times except during waste addition or inspection.
Storage areas are clearly marked with hazard signage and emergency contact information.
Maximum storage duration limits (as per Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016 – typically 90 days) are strictly monitored and documented by the EHS team.
Segregation Protocols

At Alchem International, hazardous waste is segregated based on chemical compatibility, physical properties, and risk profile to prevent reactions, fires, spills, and cross-contamination. Dedicated zones are clearly demarcated and controlled.

rows: Isolated cabinets or enclosures with mechanical ventilation, restricted access, and prominent hazard signage
Dedicated stainless-steel shelving with yellow floor and shelf markings and clear "Oxidizer" signage
Flame-proof storage cabinets or rooms with proper earthing and bonding provisions
Bundled sections with warning tape, secondary containment, and specific hazard labels
Physically segregated areas with barriers and clear incompatibility signage

body.text: Operational Practices

Hazardous waste containers are stored above ground level on polymer or chemical-resistant pallets to prevent corrosion and contact with floor spillages.
FIFO (First In, First Out) principles are strictly followed. Accumulation start dates are clearly mentioned to ensure waste is not stored beyond permitted time limits.
Daily inspections are conducted and documented by authorised personnel to check for:
Leaks, corrosion, bulging, or deterioration of containers
Integrity, accuracy, and readability of labels
Housekeeping standards and pest control status
Direction arrows, storage area layouts, emergency contact details, and GHS hazard signage are prominently displayed throughout hazardous waste storage and movement zones.

To prevent chemical burns, inhalation exposure, fire or reactivity incidents, and ergonomic injuries, Alchem International enforces strict handling procedures for all hazardous waste-related activities.
Personnel Qualification

Only trained and authorised personnel are permitted to handle hazardous waste containers.
Training covers:
Correct PPE selection, use, and limitations
Chemical compatibility, segregation rules, and incompatibility risks
Emergency spill response and use of spill kits
Fire safety measures, extinguisher use, and evacuation procedures
PPE Requirements by Waste Type

rows: Antistatic gloves, chemical splash goggles, FFP2 mask or equivalent, chemical-resistant apron, ESD safety shoes
Acid-resistant gloves, full face shield, chemical splash suit or apron, gumboots
Flame-retardant coverall, appropriate respirator, nitrile gloves, use of local exhaust ventilation or hood where required

body.text: Material Handling Tools

Dedicated trolleys with secondary containment trays for safe movement of drums and containers.
Drum lifters, grabbers, or rotators for handling large containers; manual lifting of full drums is strictly prohibited.
Spill-resistant pumps or closed transfer systems for liquid movement; manual tipping or pouring is not permitted.
Transportation of hazardous waste, both within Alchem International premises and to authorised off-site facilities, is carried out with maximum safety and regulatory control.
Internal Transfer (Within Premises)

Only approved, corrosion-resistant, and antistatic trolleys are used on designated routes.
Containers are:
Properly sealed and secured with lid locks or restraints
Covered where there is potential for vapour release or odour
Movement is preferably planned during non-peak production hours to minimise interaction with routine operations.
Routes are pre-mapped, clearly marked, and kept free from obstructions.
External Transfer (To Authorised Treatment / Disposal Facilities)

Only government-authorised transporters and vehicles are engaged (holding valid consent from SPCB/HPCB).
The EHS team prepares and verifies required waste manifests (Form 6/7 under Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016) and transport documentation in line with regulatory and customer requirements.
Containers are loaded on:
Covered vehicles with appropriate hazard placards
UN-approved sealed containers where applicable
Vehicles equipped with spill kits, MSDS folders, and emergency contact information
Disposal receipts and weight reconciliation slips are obtained and recorded in the EHS compliance system within defined timelines.
All vehicles used for hazardous waste transport must:

Be fitted with ABC-type fire extinguishers accessible to the driver and loading area.
Carry spill containment kits appropriate to the waste type.
Provide adequate ventilation to prevent vapour accumulation.
Use GPS-based tracking systems, where applicable, to enable monitoring of route adherence and transport status.
In the event of an accident, spill, leakage, fire, or any transport-related emergency involving hazardous waste:
The Transport Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is immediately activated by the transport team and EHS.
Primary actions include

Securing the area and restricting unauthorised access
Eliminating ignition sources and stopping vehicle engines where safe
Deploying spill kits to contain or neutralise the release
Using appropriate PPE based on the hazard class involved
Secondary actions include

Informing local emergency services, authorities, and medical facilities as required
Notifying the EHS Head and Site Incident Controller
Initiating internal incident reporting procedures
Following stabilisation, a detailed Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is conducted. Findings and corrective actions are recorded, and CAPA measures are implemented to prevent recurrence.
All hazardous waste transport activities form part of Alchem International's compliance and audit trail.
Transport records capture:

Transporter name, licence details, and vehicle registration
Driver details and contact information
Route and key checkpoints
Date and time of departure and arrival
Container identification numbers, waste categories, and quantities
Records are retained for a minimum of five years, or longer where required by regulations, customer requirements, or Alchem International's internal data-retention policy.

sections.title: Specialized Treatment & Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

body.text: To minimise environmental impact and reduce dependency on external disposal facilities, Alchem International implements multiple in-plant pre-treatment measures before hazardous waste is sent off-site:

pH Neutralisation Systems: Installed in extraction, purification, utilities, and maintenance wash areas. Treat acidic and alkaline wastewater generated during equipment cleaning and process washdowns. Equipped with automated pH monitoring and controlled dosing systems to bring wastewater within acceptable limits before routing to the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).
Oil & Chemical Separation Units: Used oils, greases, and oily wastewater from maintenance activities pass through oil-water separators to isolate hydrocarbons prior to further treatment or disposal.
Filtration & Adsorption Systems: Activated carbon and filtration units are used at selected discharge points to remove colour, residual chemicals, surfactants, and trace contaminants from wash water prior to ETP/STP treatment.
Solvent Recovery Systems: Distillation and purification units recover spent solvents for reuse in processes, reducing hazardous waste generation.

All hazardous waste that cannot be safely reused, recycled, or treated on-site is transferred only to government-authorised hazardous waste treatment and disposal facilities, in line with Indian environmental regulations (Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016) and customer expectations.
Treatment, Storage & Disposal Facilities (TSDF / Authorized Facilities)
Non-recoverable hazardous waste streams include:

Extraction and purification residues
ETP sludge
Spent activated carbon and filter media
Used oils and contaminated absorbents
Chemical-contaminated packaging and PPE

High-Temperature Incineration: Used for high-calorific and toxic wastes such as contaminated rags, absorbents, oily residues, and chemical sludge, ensuring destruction of hazardous constituents.
Secure Engineered Landfilling: Used for inorganic, non-recyclable hazardous solids, including filter cakes, ash, and stabilised residues, with engineered liners and leachate control systems.
Pre-Dispatch Controls
Before dispatch to authorised facilities:

Waste is fully segregated by category
Containers are sealed, labelled, and documented
Waste characteristics (where required) are reviewed to determine the appropriate treatment route
Reduction of Toxic Chemical Emissions
Alchem International adopts multiple source-level and system-level strategies to minimise hazardous emissions and reduce downstream treatment loads:

Process Parameter Optimisation: Extraction, purification, and synthesis parameters (chemical dosage, temperature, dwell time, solvent ratios) are optimised to reduce chemical losses and hazardous residues.
In-Process Recycling & Reuse: Controlled reuse of wash water, low-risk chemical streams, and internal recycling initiatives are implemented where validated and permitted.

Alchem International recognises water as a critical and finite resource that underpins its pharmaceutical, phytochemical, and nutraceutical manufacturing operations, including extraction, purification, synthesis, utilities, and domestic use. As a manufacturer supplying global markets, responsible water stewardship is central to Alchem International's sustainability strategy, regulatory compliance, customer expectations, and long-term operational resilience.

This Integrated Water Management SOP defines Alchem International's structured and comprehensive approach to water abstraction, consumption, quality monitoring, conservation, treatment, reuse, and wastewater discharge. It addresses operational and environmental risks associated with water use, including risks related to solvents, reagents, auxiliaries, oils, suspended solids, and other pharmaceutical-processing contaminants present in wastewater streams. The SOP ensures that water management is proactive, preventive, and aligned with responsible manufacturing and environmental protection principles.
The objectives of this Integrated Water Management SOP are to:

Ensure efficient, controlled, and minimised use of water across all operational areas, including production floors, extraction and purification units, utilities, laboratories, and domestic services.
Monitor, analyse, and manage wastewater responsibly through in-house Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) systems, and through authorised external discharge arrangements where applicable.
Implement source-level controls to capture, isolate, and reduce contaminants such as solvents, chemicals, oils, and suspended solids before they enter common effluent streams.
Integrate routine water audits, metered consumption tracking, and water quality monitoring into operational controls, management reviews, and sustainability reporting frameworks.
Ensure compliance with applicable local and national water regulations (Water Act, 1974; Environment Protection Act, 1986; CPCB/SPCB norms), environmental discharge standards, customer requirements, and international sustainability expectations relevant to the pharmaceutical and phytochemical industry.
This SOP applies to all departments and activities that consume water or generate wastewater, including but not limited to:

Quality Control and Inspection Areas

Water used in extraction, purification, synthesis, quality testing, and supporting production activities is metered at department or process level wherever feasible to enable consumption tracking and optimisation.
Reverse Osmosis (RO) systems used for process and utility water are operated to maximise recovery rates and minimise reject water generation, supported by preventive maintenance and membrane health monitoring.
Equipment, reactor, and floor cleaning procedures are designed using defined water quantities or validated cleaning cycles, avoiding uncontrolled free-flow washing and unnecessary water losses.

Regular preventive maintenance is carried out on cooling towers, chillers, condensers, air washers, and heat exchangers to ensure optimal thermal performance, minimise water loss due to leaks or drift, and maintain energy efficiency.

steps.heading: Leak Monitoring and Immediate Repair Protocol

body.text: Moisture sensors, level indicators, and routine visual inspections are used to detect leaks in cooling and utility water circuits. Identified leaks are logged and rectified within 24 hours to prevent water wastage and operational disruption.

Where technically and economically feasible, Alchem International operates closed-loop cooling systems for chillers and process equipment, reducing blowdown losses, preventing contamination, and minimising wastewater discharge from cooling operations.

Cooling intensity is automatically adjusted based on real-time production load, ambient conditions, and machine requirements through control systems, preventing overcooling and unnecessary water and energy consumption.

Water-efficient alternatives such as air-cooled chillers, hybrid cooling systems, drift eliminators, and high-efficiency tower internals are implemented or evaluated to reduce reliance on water-intensive cooling methods.

Technologies such as Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), improved insulation, condensate recovery, and optimised pump operations are used to simultaneously reduce water abstraction and electricity consumption.

Daily and monthly logs covering make-up water usage, blowdown volumes, cycles of concentration, and energy consumption are maintained to identify inefficiencies and support continuous improvement initiatives.

Pre-treatment of process wastewater from extraction, purification, and synthesis operations is carried out using:
Activated carbon filters for colour and organic load reduction
pH neutralisation tanks to correct acidic or alkaline streams
Solvent recovery and separation units
Chemical-laden liquid waste (e.g., high-strength extraction residues, spent solvents) is segregated at source, stored in labelled containers, and handed over to authorised hazardous waste handlers instead of being mixed with general effluent.
All industrial wastewater is routed to the in-house Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and domestic wastewater to the Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), where appropriate physical, chemical, and biological treatment processes are employed to reduce pollutants.
Where applicable, treated effluent meeting prescribed standards is discharged to an authorised Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) or approved discharge points, ensuring compliance with regulatory norms.
Greywater streams, including RO reject, cooling tower blowdown (where permissible), and wash water from handwash stations, are collected separately and reused for non-critical applications such as toilet flushing, floor cleaning, or gardening (where permitted).
Alchem International maintains formal agreements with authorised CETP operators and treatment partners, supported by periodic effluent sampling and testing through accredited laboratories (NABL/MoEFCC-approved) to verify compliance.

No untreated or partially treated industrial or domestic wastewater is discharged to soil, open drains, or natural water bodies. This requirement is strictly enforced across all facilities.
Effluent is managed through closed collection systems and routed only to authorised treatment facilities (ETP/STP/CETP).
Secondary containment such as trays and drip pans are installed beneath chemical storage, extraction chemical areas, fuel storage, and critical equipment.
Spill kits containing absorbents, neutralisers, and booms are positioned at strategic locations for immediate response.
Containment systems, bunds, trenches, and barriers are inspected periodically to ensure integrity.
Groundwater abstraction (where applicable) is monitored monthly, and groundwater levels and quality are reviewed annually through internal checks or third-party testing, in compliance with Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) guidelines.

blocks.text: Context and Commitment

Alchem International is committed to minimizing freshwater consumption and reducing wastewater pollution arising from extraction, purification, cleaning, and finishing operations associated with pharmaceutical manufacturing. As an India-based facility operating in a water-stressed region (Faridabad, Haryana), the company prioritizes water efficiency, chemical optimization, and pollution prevention as core environmental performance objectives.
This integrated approach focuses on reducing water use at source, improving cleaning efficiency, and limiting the discharge of high-impact chemicals, including those contributing to AOX in wastewater.

sections.title: Water Efficiency, Low-Impact Processing, and Responsible Cleaning Practices

body.text:
Alchem International has implemented optimized cleaning and washing practices to reduce excessive water consumption without compromising product quality or workplace hygiene. Traditional high-volume wash practices are replaced, where feasible, with controlled and efficient cleaning methods.
Key measures include the use of low-flow nozzles, pressure-assisted cleaning equipment, and optimized wash cycles that limit water use to only what is operationally necessary. Cleaning processes are standardized through defined work instructions to avoid prolonged or repeated washing.
Sequential washing practices are applied so that lightly contaminated rinse water may be reused for initial cleaning stages, reducing overall freshwater demand.

Cleaning processes are designed with defined parameters for time, pressure, temperature, and chemical concentration. Operators follow approved work instructions that prevent over-washing, uncontrolled hose use, or unnecessary re-cleaning.
Routine monitoring of water consumption helps identify deviations and improvement opportunities, while maintenance checks ensure that valves, hoses, and spray systems remain leak-free and efficient.

In parallel with water reduction initiatives, Alchem International actively works to minimize AOx load in wastewater by reducing the use of chlorine-based chemicals and sodium chlorate in cleaning, bleaching, or purification-related applications.
Where technically feasible, alternative low-AOx or non-chlorinated chemicals are used. Chemical selection decisions prioritize environmental compatibility, lower toxicity, and reduced halogen content.
Controlled chemical dosing systems ensure accurate application, preventing excess chemical discharge during washing or cleaning stages.

Water-efficient machinery and fixtures are installed in relevant production and cleaning areas. These include controlled spray systems, recirculation-supported wash units, and equipment designed to deliver effective cleaning with reduced water volumes.
Installation records and equipment manuals are maintained to demonstrate correct setup, operation, and maintenance of water-saving systems.

Alchem International maintains operational efficiency reports tracking water consumption trends, cleaning process performance, and chemical usage. These records support internal reviews and provide documented evidence for audits and customer assessments.
Effluent parameters are periodically reviewed to assess the effectiveness of water-saving and low-AOx measures, ensuring alignment with regulatory limits and customer expectations.

blocks.text:
Alchem International recognises that maintaining clean air within and around its manufacturing facilities is a critical element of environmental stewardship, worker health and safety, and responsible community engagement. As a pharmaceutical and phytochemical manufacturer, Alchem International operates a range of activities—including extraction, purification, synthesis, utilities, and material handling—that can generate air emissions such as dust, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), chemical vapours, combustion gases, odours, and noise if not properly managed.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the preventive strategies, engineering controls, monitoring systems, and management practices adopted by Alchem International to control atmospheric emissions, process-generated vapours, workplace dust, odours, and noise. These measures are designed to ensure compliance with applicable environmental and occupational health regulations—including the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, and CPCB/SPCB norms—meet international customer expectations, and protect employees, neighbouring communities, and the surrounding environment.
The objectives of this SOP are to:

Prevent and minimise emissions of VOCs, particulate matter, chemical vapours, and combustion gases from production and utility operations.
Monitor indoor air quality, process emissions, and ambient air quality at regular intervals and take prompt corrective action in case of deviations.
Minimise workplace and boundary-level noise generated from utilities and production machinery through engineering and administrative controls.
Control and mitigate nuisance odours arising from extraction, purification, chemical storage, wastewater treatment, and waste handling activities.
Maintain full compliance with applicable environmental regulations, occupational hygiene standards, and customer environmental and social responsibility requirements relevant to the pharmaceutical and phytochemical industry.
This SOP applies to:

All manufacturing operations involving chemical usage, extraction, purification, synthesis, heating, drying, ventilation, or exhaust systems.
All personnel involved in production activities, operation of fume hoods and local exhaust ventilation (LEV), chemical handling, material transfer, and waste handling.
All noise- and emission-generating equipment, including utilities (boilers, generators, compressors, chillers, cooling towers), production machinery, dust extraction systems, and exhaust stacks at Alchem International facilities.

responsibilities: Develop and implement air emission and noise monitoring programmes; assess emission risks; consolidate monitoring data; ensure compliance with statutory limits and customer requirements; and drive corrective and preventive actions.

Scrubbers are designed to neutralise odorous compounds and chemical vapours. Scrubber performance is verified through routine monitoring of pH, conductivity, and total dissolved solids (TDS) of recirculating scrubbing liquor.

Chemical preparation, mixing, and transfer activities are carried out in enclosed or semi-enclosed systems wherever feasible. Containers are kept sealed, and vapours are routed to exhaust and treatment systems to minimise fugitive emissions.

LEV systems are installed at high-risk points such as reactors, distillation units, chemical dosing areas, and maintenance workstations. These systems capture vapours and dust at source and discharge them through filtration or scrubbing units.

Activated carbon-based adsorption units are deployed in selected high-VOC areas such as solvent storage rooms and chemical handling zones. Carbon media is monitored for breakthrough and replaced or regenerated as per defined schedules.

Routine inspections are conducted to identify leaks from pipelines, valves, pumps, chemical containers, and exhaust ducts. Detected leaks or abnormal odours are logged, investigated, and rectified within defined corrective action timelines.

Emissions from boilers, generators, and thermic fluid heaters are controlled through proper burner design, fuel quality control, optimised combustion settings, and regular tuning to minimise NOx, SOx, CO, and particulate emissions.

Utility and process stacks are designed in accordance with regulatory guidelines for height and exit velocity to ensure effective dispersion. Sampling ports and safe access platforms are provided for stack emission monitoring.

Where applicable, continuous or periodic monitoring is carried out for parameters such as particulate matter, SOx, NOx, CO, and VOCs. Alert thresholds trigger immediate investigation and corrective action if values approach permissible limits.

Ambient air quality monitoring is conducted at designated upwind and downwind boundary locations to assess PM2.5, PM10, VOCs, NOx, SOx, and other relevant parameters. Trends are reviewed periodically and benchmarked against applicable ambient air quality standards to ensure negligible off-site impact.

blocks.text: At Alchem International, particulate matter (PM) generated from pharmaceutical manufacturing, material handling, utilities, and material movement is managed through layered engineering controls, real-time monitoring, and preventive maintenance to protect worker health, ensure regulatory compliance, and prevent off-site impacts.

steps.heading: Baghouse Dust Collectors with HEPA-Grade Filters

body.text: Baghouse systems fitted with high-efficiency (HEPA-grade) filters are installed on particulate-generating equipment such as dryers, mills, blenders, and material handling points where fine powders and dust are generated. These systems provide filtration efficiency exceeding 99.9% for fine particulates, maintaining clean work environments and controlling stack emissions.

steps.heading: Wet Scrubbing Systems with Packed Bed Columns

body.text: Wet scrubbers are connected to exhausts from extraction, purification, and chemical preparation areas where mist, aerosols, or particulate-bound vapours may be generated. Scrubber effectiveness is assessed through pressure drop monitoring, pH checks, conductivity/TDS trends, and visual inspections of packing media and spray distribution.

ESPs are deployed on boiler stacks and other high-temperature exhaust sources to remove sub-micron particulate matter (< 1 μm). ESP performance indicators—including inlet/outlet dust load, voltage (kV), spark rate, and plate condition—are reviewed and documented during quarterly EHS and engineering audits.

PM10 and PM2.5 sensors are installed at critical exhaust ducts and selected ambient monitoring locations. These sensors are integrated with alarm-linked control panels that alert operators to abnormal emission spikes, triggering immediate investigation, load reduction, or controlled shutdown actions.
All particulate control systems follow defined maintenance schedules, including:

Daily or shift-wise pulse-jet cleaning (where applicable)
Weekly filter and hopper inspections
Periodic fan, motor, damper, and duct integrity checks
Calibration of differential pressure gauges and sensors to ensure sustained capture efficiency

sections.title: CO, SO₂, NOₓ and Heavy Metal Emission Mitigation

body.text: Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) are installed on major stacks associated with boilers, generators, thermic fluid heaters, and key exhaust systems. Parameters monitored include SO₂, NOₓ, CO, CO₂, particulate matter, and VOCs where applicable.

AAQMS units are installed at strategic perimeter locations to monitor PM10, PM2.5, NOₓ, SOₓ, CO, and VOCs. The EHS team reviews monitoring data weekly or monthly, depending on operational risk levels.

Manual stack emission testing is conducted at least quarterly by accredited third-party laboratories (NABL/MoEFCC-approved). Parameters tested include SO₂, NOₓ, CO, particulate matter, and total VOCs, with results certified and retained for compliance reporting.

Emission and ambient air data are consolidated into an Environmental Data Management System. Analytics tools evaluate trends, detect anomalies, and auto-generate alarms when values approach defined action thresholds, enabling prompt corrective measures.
VOC emissions from chemical storage, extraction, purification, and maintenance activities are minimised through:

Vapour balancing and return lines
Enclosed chemical transfer systems
Activated carbon adsorption units
Optimised ventilation and exhaust capture
Operational parameters are adjusted based on monitoring data to further reduce fugitive releases.

Sulphur-emitting processes are fully enclosed using sealed reactors, ducts, and processing chambers to prevent fugitive emissions.
Exhaust air from processing units is routed through sulphur absorption and recovery equipment rather than being released directly into the atmosphere.
The closed-loop system allows sulphur vapors to be captured, neutralized, and recovered for reuse or safe disposal.
Negative pressure is maintained within enclosed areas to prevent leakage into the work environment.

Dedicated emission control equipment is installed to absorb sulphur compounds through chemical scrubbing or adsorption media.
Recovered sulphur or sulphur-containing solutions are either reused in controlled processes or managed as per approved waste handling procedures.
The system operates continuously during sulphur-related production activities to ensure uninterrupted emission control.

Standard operating procedures define start-up, operation, monitoring, and shutdown of sulphur recovery systems.
Emission control equipment performance is monitored through operational efficiency checks and process parameters.
Process optimization initiatives are implemented to reduce sulphur losses and improve recovery rates.

Alchem International recognises that odour emissions from pharmaceutical, phytochemical, and nutraceutical manufacturing operations can cause nuisance, discomfort, and complaints from neighbouring communities, employees, and other stakeholders. Odours may arise from various sources including botanical raw material processing, solvent handling, extraction and purification operations, effluent treatment, waste storage, and chemical reactions. These odours, if not properly controlled, can impact community relations, regulatory compliance, and the company's social licence to operate.

This Odor Control & Filtration Management System Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes Alchem International's structured framework for the identification, prevention, capture, treatment, and monitoring of odorous emissions from all manufacturing and support operations. The SOP focuses on the installation, maintenance, and replacement of odour-minimizing filters and associated air pollution control equipment to prevent the release of odours to the company's premises and surrounding environment.

Aligned with applicable environmental regulations in India—including the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, CPCB/SPCB guidelines on odour control, and the Environment Protection Act, 1986—as well as international best practices and customer expectations, this SOP ensures that odour emissions are managed responsibly and effectively.
The objectives of this Odor Control & Filtration Management System SOP are to:

Identify all significant odour sources across Alchem International manufacturing facilities and operations.
Prevent and minimise the generation of odorous compounds through process optimisation, material substitution, and operational controls.
Capture and treat odorous emissions at source using appropriate filtration, scrubbing, and adsorption technologies.
Install, maintain, and replace odour-minimizing filters on a regular and defined schedule to ensure continuous effective odour control.
Monitor odour emissions and ambient odour levels at facility boundaries and sensitive receptor locations.
Ensure compliance with applicable odour regulations, CPCB/SPCB norms, and customer requirements.
Respond promptly to odour complaints and incidents through investigation and corrective action.
Protect the health, safety, and comfort of employees, neighbouring communities, and other stakeholders.

All Alchem International manufacturing facilities, production units, and operational areas that may generate odorous emissions, including:

Botanical Raw Material Handling and Storage Areas

blocks.text: Alchem International employs a multi-barrier approach for odour capture and treatment, combining multiple technologies based on odour source characteristics and treatment requirements.

body.text: LEV systems are installed at odour-generating points to capture odours at source and prevent their release into the workplace and environment.
Design and Installation

LEV systems are designed based on odour source characteristics, capture velocity requirements, and airflow needs.
Hoods, ducts, and fans are sized and positioned to ensure effective capture of odorous emissions.
LEV systems are integrated with odour treatment equipment (filters, scrubbers, biofilters) for comprehensive control.
Operation and Maintenance

LEV systems are operated continuously during odour-generating activities.
Airflow and capture efficiency are verified periodically.
Filters, ducts, and fans are inspected and maintained as per defined schedules.
Performance issues are addressed promptly to prevent odour release.

Odour-minimizing filters are installed in LEV systems, exhaust ducts, and air handling units to remove odorous compounds from air streams before release. These filters are maintained and replaced on a regular basis to ensure continuous effective odour control.
Types of Odour-Minimizing Filters

Activated Carbon Filters: Activated carbon is highly effective for adsorption of a wide range of odorous organic compounds, including solvents, VOCs, and sulphur compounds.
Activated Carbon Impregnated with Chemicals: Chemically impregnated activated carbon (e.g., with potassium hydroxide, potassium iodide, or sulphur) is used for enhanced removal of specific odorous compounds such as H₂S, ammonia, and amines.
HEPA Filters: High-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters remove particulate-bound odours and fine dust.
ULPA Filters: Ultra-low penetration air (ULPA) filters provide higher filtration efficiency for fine particulates and odours.
Zeolite Filters: Zeolites are used for adsorption of specific odorous compounds, including ammonia and volatile organic compounds.
Biofilters: Biofilters use microbial action to degrade odorous compounds and are effective for organic odours.
Filter Installation

Odour-minimizing filters are installed at all identified odour sources, including LEV exhausts, stack emissions, and air handling units serving odour-prone areas.
Filters are selected based on odour characteristics, airflow rate, and treatment objectives.
Filters are installed in appropriately designed housings with proper sealing to prevent bypass.
Installation records are maintained, including filter type, size, location, and installation date.
Filter Maintenance and Replacement

Regular Inspection: Odour-minimizing filters are inspected at defined intervals (e.g., weekly, monthly) to check for: Physical damage, clogging, or saturation; Pressure drop across the filter; Airflow and capture efficiency; Sign of odour breakthrough
Performance Monitoring: Filter performance is monitored through: Pressure drop measurements; Odour detection at exhaust outlets; Regular odour monitoring at facility boundaries; Analytical testing for specific odorous compounds
Filter Replacement Schedule: Filters are replaced on a defined schedule based on: Manufacturer recommendations; Operating hours; Pressure drop thresholds; Odour breakthrough detection; Regular inspection findings
Replacement Frequency: As a general guideline: Activated carbon filters: Every 3–6 months or when breakthrough is detected; HEPA/ULPA filters: Every 6–12 months or when pressure drop exceeds limits; Zeolite filters: Every 6–12 months or as per manufacturer recommendations; Biofilter media: Every 12–24 months or when performance degrades
Documentation: Filter replacement activities are documented, including: Filter type and location; Date of replacement; Reason for replacement; New filter specifications; Disposal method for spent filters
Spent Filter Management

Spent odour-minimizing filters are managed as hazardous or non-hazardous waste based on their contamination.
Spent activated carbon is sent to authorised recyclers or regenerators where feasible.
Contaminated filters are disposed of through authorised waste disposal facilities.
Disposal records are maintained for compliance and audit purposes.
Wet scrubbers are used to remove water-soluble odorous compounds and particulate matter from air streams. They are particularly effective for acidic or alkaline odours.
Types of Wet Scrubbers

Packed Bed Scrubbers: Use packing media to provide a large surface area for gas-liquid contact.
Venturi Scrubbers: Use high-velocity gas flow to atomise scrubbing liquid and capture fine particulates.
Spray Tower Scrubbers: Use spray nozzles to create fine droplets for gas absorption.
Impingement Scrubbers: Use impingement plates to create turbulence and enhance gas-liquid contact.
Operation and Maintenance

Scrubbing liquid (water, caustic, acid, or oxidizing solution) is selected based on odour characteristics.
Scrubbing liquid pH, concentration, and flow rate are monitored and maintained.
Packing media, nozzles, and mist eliminators are inspected and cleaned regularly.
Blowdown and make-up water are managed to maintain scrubbing efficiency.
Performance is monitored through pH, pressure drop, and odour removal efficiency.
Biofilters use microbial action to degrade odorous organic compounds. They are effective for a wide range of organic odours and are environmentally friendly.
Design and Operation

Biofilters consist of a filter bed (e.g., compost, wood chips, or synthetic media) with microbial populations.
Odorous air is passed through the filter bed, where microorganisms degrade odorous compounds.
Moisture, temperature, pH, and nutrient levels are maintained for optimal microbial activity.
Biofilters are designed based on airflow rate, odour characteristics, and required removal efficiency.
Maintenance

Media is inspected periodically for compaction, channeling, and drying.
Moisture is maintained through irrigation systems.
Nutrients are supplemented as needed to support microbial growth.
Media is replaced or replenished when performance degrades.
Performance is monitored through odour removal efficiency and microbial activity.
Thermal oxidisers are used for destruction of odorous compounds at high temperatures. They are effective for high-concentration, high-flow odour streams.
Types of Thermal Oxidisers

Direct-Fired Thermal Oxidisers: Use direct flame contact for odour destruction.
Regenerative Thermal Oxidisers (RTOs): Use heat recovery for energy efficiency.
Catalytic Thermal Oxidisers: Use catalysts to lower oxidation temperature.
Operation and Maintenance

Operating temperature, residence time, and oxygen concentration are monitored and controlled.
Burners, heat exchangers, and catalysts are inspected and maintained.
Performance is monitored through odour removal efficiency and emission monitoring.
Energy consumption is optimised through heat recovery and process integration.
Activated carbon adsorption systems are used for removal of a wide range of odorous organic compounds.
Design and Operation

Activated carbon is selected based on odour characteristics and treatment requirements.
Adsorption systems are designed with appropriate contact time, airflow rate, and carbon quantity.
Multiple beds are used for continuous operation during carbon replacement.
Performance is monitored through odour removal efficiency and carbon exhaustion.
Maintenance

Carbon is replaced based on breakthrough detection or scheduled intervals.
Spent carbon is regenerated or disposed of through authorised facilities.
System pressure drop and airflow are monitored to detect clogging or channeling.

Parameters: Odour concentration, intensity, character, and hedonic tone.

Ambient odour monitoring is conducted at facility boundaries and sensitive receptor locations to assess off-site odour impact.

Odour Complaint Management
Alchem International maintains a structured odour complaint management system to receive, investigate, and respond to odour complaints from employees, neighbours, and other stakeholders.
Complaint Receipt

Complaints may be received through: Direct communication (phone, email, in-person); Community grievance mechanisms; Regulatory authorities; Employee reports
All complaints are logged in the Odour Complaint Register with details including date, time, location, description, and complainant information.
Complaint Investigation

EHS team acknowledges complaints within 24 hours and initiates investigation.
Investigation includes: Site inspection of odour sources; Review of odour control equipment performance; Meteorological conditions assessment; Sampling and analysis if required; Interviews with relevant personnel
Root cause analysis is conducted to identify the source and cause of the odour.

Corrective actions are documented, and their effectiveness is verified.

The complainant is informed of the investigation findings and corrective actions.
Follow-up is conducted to ensure the issue is resolved and no further complaints are received.
Complaint trends are reviewed periodically to identify recurring issues and improvement opportunities.

blocks.text: Alchem International recognises that accurate demand forecasting and responsible inventory management are critical to minimising the risk of overproduction, excess inventories of unused or expired pharmaceutical products, and the eventual release of pharmaceutical compounds to the environment. As a manufacturer of APIs, botanical extracts, and nutraceutical ingredients serving global markets, Alchem International must balance the need to meet customer demand reliably with the imperative to minimise waste, reduce environmental impact, and optimise resource utilisation.
Overproduction and excess inventory in the pharmaceutical industry can lead to:

Expiration of pharmaceutical products, requiring costly and environmentally sensitive disposal.
Increased risk of environmental release of pharmaceutical compounds through improper disposal.
Unnecessary consumption of raw materials, energy, and water.
Increased storage and handling costs.
Potential regulatory non-compliance and financial losses.
Contribution to the global challenge of pharmaceutical waste in the environment.

This Pharmaceutical Demand Forecasting & Responsible Inventory Management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes Alchem International's structured framework, tools, and strategies for estimating demand for pharmaceutical products, optimising inventory levels, and minimising the risk of overproduction and pharmaceutical waste. The SOP aligns with Indian regulatory requirements, customer expectations, and international best practices for responsible pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Improve production planning and resource utilisation through accurate demand forecasting.

blocks.text: Alchem International employs a range of tools and strategies to estimate demand for pharmaceutical products accurately and minimise the risk of overproduction and excess inventory.

body.text:
Order History Analysis: Analysis of historical order data, including order quantities, frequencies, seasonality, and customer patterns.
Sales Trend Analysis: Analysis of sales trends over time to identify growth, decline, or cyclical patterns.
Customer Segmentation: Segmentation of customers based on order patterns, product preferences, and demand characteristics.
Product Lifecycle Analysis: Analysis of product lifecycle stages (introduction, growth, maturity, decline) to anticipate demand changes.
Data Sources: ERP systems, sales records, customer databases, and historical production data.

Customer Forecasts: Collection and integration of customer forecasts, contracts, and demand commitments.
Customer Collaboration: Regular engagement with customers on demand planning, product requirements, and market trends.
Contract Analysis: Analysis of customer contracts for committed volumes, delivery schedules, and pricing.
Customer Relationship Management (CRM): Use of CRM systems to track customer interactions, requirements, and forecasts.
Demand Sensing: Use of real-time customer signals to adjust forecasts dynamically.

Time Series Analysis: Use of statistical methods (moving average, exponential smoothing, ARIMA) to forecast demand based on historical patterns.
Regression Analysis: Use of regression models to identify relationships between demand and influencing factors (e.g., price, seasonality, economic indicators).
Causal Models: Use of causal models to forecast demand based on underlying drivers.
Simulation Models: Use of simulation to evaluate different demand scenarios and their impact on production and inventory.
Forecast Accuracy Tracking: Regular tracking of forecast accuracy and adjustment of models as needed.

Market Research: Collection and analysis of market data, industry trends, and competitive intelligence.
Regulatory Intelligence: Monitoring of regulatory changes that may impact demand (e.g., new approvals, patent expirations, regulatory restrictions).
Economic Indicators: Analysis of economic indicators (GDP, inflation, exchange rates) that may impact demand.
Seasonal Trends: Analysis of seasonal patterns in demand for different products.
Emerging Trends: Identification of emerging trends (e.g., new therapeutic areas, changing consumer preferences) that may impact demand.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaboration between Business Development, Production Planning, Supply Chain, and Finance on demand forecasting.
Customer Collaboration: Collaboration with key customers on demand planning and replenishment.
Supplier Collaboration: Collaboration with key suppliers on lead times, capacity, and delivery schedules.
Regular Review Meetings: Monthly or quarterly review meetings to align forecasts and plans.
Information Sharing: Sharing of demand forecasts, inventory data, and production plans across the supply chain.

ERP Systems: Use of ERP systems for demand planning, inventory management, and production planning.
Advanced Planning Systems (APS): Use of APS for demand forecasting, production scheduling, and inventory optimization.
Spreadsheet Models: Use of spreadsheet models for demand forecasting and scenario analysis.
Business Intelligence (BI) Tools: Use of BI tools for data analysis, visualization, and reporting.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML): Use of AI/ML algorithms for improved demand forecasting accuracy.

Scenario Analysis: Development of different demand scenarios (best case, base case, worst case) to evaluate production and inventory strategies.
Sensitivity Analysis: Analysis of demand sensitivity to key variables (e.g., price, customer demand, regulatory changes).
Risk Assessment: Identification and assessment of risks that may impact demand (e.g., supply chain disruptions, regulatory changes, market shifts).
Contingency Planning: Development of contingency plans to address demand variability and uncertainty.
Flexibility and Agility: Design of production and supply chain systems to be flexible and responsive to demand changes.

blocks.text: Alchem International employs responsible inventory management strategies to balance supply security with waste reduction.

body.text:

VED Analysis: Classification of inventory based on criticality (V = vital, E = essential, D = desirable).

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the mandatory requirements for the safe handling, storage, transfer, use, and disposal of chemicals at all Alchem International Private Limited facilities. These injuries may affect muscles, tendons, nerves, joints, and other soft tissues. Activities such as reactor charging, drum handling, filtration, packing, quality inspection, laboratory analysis, and computer-based work are associated with ergonomic risk factors. Alchem International Private Limited operates manufacturing facilities that handle high-value pharmaceutical actives, controlled substances, proprietary botanical extracts, and sensitive intellectual property. Security personnel are deployed to protect people, assets, and information. However, the presence of security personnel also creates a power dynamic that—if misused—can result in fear, intimidation, coercion, and human rights violations.

This SOP exists to draw a clear, enforceable line: security personnel are protectors, not disciplinarians. They safeguard life, property, and dignity. They do not punish, discipline, restrain, or humiliate. This SOP defines prohibited conduct, the narrow conditions under which force may ever be used, and the accountability mechanisms that ensure violations are detected and addressed.

The UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials
The UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
The Factories Act, 1948
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023
ILO Convention 190 on Violence and Harassment
Customer social compliance requirements (PSCI, Sedex, EcoVadis)

blocks.text: Alchem International Private Limited is entrusted with confidential, proprietary, and sensitive information by employees, customers, buyers, suppliers, contractors, auditors, regulators, and other stakeholders. As a manufacturer operating within the pharmaceutical, phytochemical, nutraceutical, and cosmeceutical value chain—serving global customers with strict compliance, quality, and social responsibility expectations—robust data governance is essential to ensure regulatory compliance, operational integrity, and stakeholder trust.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes structured requirements for the collection, processing, storage, safeguarding, retention, and secure disposal of confidential information. It aligns with:

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP Act), 2023
The Information Technology Act, 2000 and IT (Reasonable Security Practices) Rules, 2011
The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940
Customer confidentiality agreements
ISO 27001 principles
Contractual confidentiality obligations
Applicable international data protection requirements
This SOP aims to:

Ensure that all confidential and sensitive data is collected and processed lawfully, transparently, and for legitimate business purposes.
Protect internal and third-party data through controlled access, secure IT systems, physical safeguards, and monitored handling practices.
Establish a clear and compliant record retention schedule aligned with statutory, customer, audit, and business requirements.
Maintain transparency by informing stakeholders how their data is collected, used, stored, shared, and retained.
Restrict access to confidential information through role-based permissions, need-to-know principles, and data minimisation.
Continuously review and strengthen data protection measures to address emerging risks, regulatory updates, and technological changes.
Provide defined internal channels for employees and stakeholders to raise queries or concerns related to data privacy and handling.
Ensure secure, irreversible destruction of records once retention periods expire, preventing unauthorised recovery or misuse.

blocks.text: Alchem International recognizes that environmental disruptions—whether acute (floods, cyclones, heat waves, earthquakes) or chronic (water scarcity, rising temperatures, ecosystem degradation)—can cause significant operational, financial, and reputational damage. To withstand and recover from such disruptions, the company has established a structured framework of contingency measures that ensure financial stability, maintain basic operations, and protect stakeholder interests.

This SOP outlines the operational buffers, financial safety nets, and contingency mechanisms in place at Alchem International to maintain business continuity during and immediately after a severe climate event or disruption of ecosystem services. Establish contingency measures to withstand and recover from environmental disruptions.

blocks.text:
Alchem International is committed to conducting all sensitive, exceptional, or high-risk transactions with the highest standards of integrity, transparency, accountability, and regulatory compliance. As a manufacturer and exporter operating within global pharmaceutical, phytochemical, and nutraceutical supply chains, Alchem International recognizes that certain transactions may pose elevated financial, ethical, operational, or reputational risks if not governed through a structured approval framework.

This protocol establishes a formal, traceable, and auditable system to evaluate, authorize, execute, and document sensitive transactions. It reinforces Alchem International's governance commitments under ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety), ISO 37001 (Anti-Bribery Management Systems), customer compliance expectations, and internationally accepted principles related to ethical conduct, anti-corruption, and responsible business practices.

This protocol is designed to:

Define a standardized, transparent, and traceable decision-making process for all sensitive transactions.
Prevent bribery, favoritism, undue influence, or conflicts of interest that may compromise business integrity.
Ensure thorough financial, legal, regulatory, and ethical evaluation prior to approval.
Strengthen internal oversight while enabling timely and compliant decision-making.
Maintain accurate documentation to support internal audits, external audits, buyer assessments, and stakeholder assurance.
Ensure compliance with applicable anti-corruption laws and customer requirements.
Protect Alchem International's reputation and stakeholder trust.

This SOP applies to all Alchem International employees, managers, consultants, and contract personnel involved in initiating, reviewing, recommending, or approving sensitive transactions.

rows: Capital expenditure, large procurement, major contracts

Alchem International is committed to maintaining the highest standards of information security, data privacy, operational continuity, and ethical business conduct across all its manufacturing, administrative, and supply-chain operations. As a pharmaceutical and phytochemical manufacturing organization serving international customers, brands, and compliance-driven markets, the protection of confidential business information, employee data, customer specifications, and operational systems is essential for maintaining trust, regulatory compliance, and uninterrupted production.

This Incident Response Procedure (IRP) establishes a structured, timely, and traceable approach for identifying, reporting, containing, investigating, and resolving information security, data privacy, and operational system incidents. steps.heading: Step 1: Immediate Action by First Responder

body.text: Any employee who discovers or suspects an incident must act immediately.

substeps.text: Treat All Incidents as High Priority: Unusual system behavior, missing files, unauthorized access alerts, suspicious emails, data leakage, or physical document loss must never be ignored.

Contain the Incident (If Safe to Do So): Disconnect affected systems from the network. Log out of compromised user accounts. Stop active data transfers or unauthorized access. Remove external storage devices involved.

Notify the Incident Response Team (IRT) Immediately: Incidents must be reported through any available internal channel: Designated incident reporting email; IT / Compliance contact number; Internal reporting form or ERP alert; Direct phone or WhatsApp message to IT, HR, or Compliance.

Document Critical Details: The reporter must record: Date and time of discovery; Location (office, factory floor, server, system, file cabinet, etc.); Systems or documents affected; Actions already taken; Visible or suspected impact.
Preserve Evidence: Do not delete files, logs, emails, or CCTV footage. Do not reset devices unless instructed. Do not attempt independent fixes or data recovery.

body.text: Severity Assessment: Incidents are classified as:

rows: Data breach involving employee data, buyer information, payroll, cyberattack, ransomware, system sabotage, theft of records
Ransomware, data exfiltration, unauthorized access to sensitive files

substeps.text: Containment Measures: Disable affected user accounts. Block unauthorized network access. Isolate affected devices or systems. Secure physical locations or document storage.

Internal Notifications: Inform relevant stakeholders: HR; IT; Compliance; Department Heads; Senior Management.

Escalation (If Required): Engage: External IT security or forensic experts; Legal advisors; Law enforcement (for theft, sabotage, or criminal acts); Buyer-mandated reporting channels where contractually required.

body.text: Internal Communication: Employees are informed strictly on a need-to-know basis. Instructions are issued to prevent further risk. Confidentiality is reinforced to avoid rumors or misinformation.

Media & Public Communication: Handled exclusively by: Managing Director / CEO; Authorized Senior Management Representative. Unauthorized disclosure is strictly prohibited.
The Compliance and Legal teams will:

Within 15 working days of assessment closure:

Department-wise assessment reports and compliance scorecards are prepared.

Reports include:

Compliance percentage
Key gaps and observations
Good practices identified
Risk exposure levels
Recommended corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs)
Reports are shared with Department Heads, the Management Review Committee, and the Compliance function.

Each department must submit a CAPA plan within 10 working days of receiving the assessment report.

CAPAs are tracked through a centralized tracker capturing:

Responsible owner
Target completion date
Current status
Verification remarks
Progress is reviewed monthly, and delays or recurring non-compliances are escalated to Senior Management.
At the end of the assessment cycle:

The IAC prepares a consolidated Internal Assessment Summary Report.
The report is presented during the annual Management Review Meeting (MRM) and highlights:
Key compliance risks
Trend analysis across departments
Recurring gaps and systemic issues
Department-wise performance
Strategic improvement priorities for the next cycle

All assessment data—especially related to ethics, discrimination, harassment, or whistleblower matters—is treated as strictly confidential. Access is restricted to the IAC, Compliance, HR, and Senior Management only.
